sentences.text: Deep in the green canopy, many creatures make their homes.
The jungle is packed with diverse wildlife, including chameleons, toucans, sloths, and jaguars.
Each of these animals has special traits that help them survive.
Scientists study these living things to learn how the forest works.
Protecting this habitat is important for all species.

sentences.text: Rainforest animals have clever ways to stay safe from predators.
Many insects use camouflage, such as turning green to match the leaves or looking like a brown twig.
This disguise keeps them hidden from hungry birds.
Even larger animals sometimes use colors to blend in with trees.
Staying unseen is the best defense in the wild.

sentences.text: Rainforests receive a lot of rain throughout the year.
Because of this wet climate, the forest floor is full of rotting logs and damp soil.
Decomposers, for example mushrooms, earthworms, and bacteria, break down this dead material.
This process recycles important nutrients back into the dirt.
Without these organisms, the jungle would quickly pile up with waste.
